claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means do you live with him and pay for things like his food, clothing, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I pay for everything - his food, clothes, all his day-to-day needs. I'm fully responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or equivalent qualifications at school or college?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't doing A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex registered with either the careers service or Connexions service?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me just confirm a couple more details:

**Does anyone else currently receive Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else also responsible for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - he lives with me and I'm the one looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit can be claimed for children under 16, or for young people aged 16 to 19 if they are in approved full-time non-advanced education or training. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in education, training, or registered with careers services, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

**However**, if Alex's circumstances change and he decides to return to education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications) or enters approved training, you could become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him at that point, up until he turns 20.

If you have any other questions or if Alex's situation changes, please feel free to ask.
